item.title: COP31 Nears Close as ‘Weak’, ‘Compromised’ Draft Draws Fierce Backlash
item.description: Civil society organisations and delegates from climate-vulnerable countries have sharply criticised the latest draft of the Presidency-led cover decision at the UN climate summit. item.title: Genocide Ruling Against Myanmar Sparks Rohingya Celebrations
item.description: Cheers and celebrations erupted in mass refugee camps across the border from Myanmar on Thursday as a landmark world court ruling found the military regime had committed genocide against its Rohingya minority. item.title: Kenya Contained Ebola With Preparation, Not Luck. Africa Needs More of the Same
item.description: Last week, on 11 November, Kenya discharged its last Ebola patient, just 37 days after the country recorded the first-ever case of the virus in its territory. If no new cases emerge over the next six weeks, Kenya will be officially declared Ebola free on 23 December. So far, zero community transmission has been recorded […]

item.title: No government approval needed to form or join a group, UN rights committee says
item.description: People do not need their government’s permission to form or join an association, the UN Human Rights Committee said on Thursday, issuing new guidance as civic space shrinks around the world.

item.title: World’s top court finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
item.description: The International Court of Justice, the principal judicial organ of the UN, delivered its judgment on Thursday in the case of The Gambia v. Myanmar on the application of the Genocide Convention, finding Myanmar responsible for the crime against the country’s ethnic Rohingya, the first such ruling against a State.

item.title: COP31: Ambition goes missing as fossil fuel language drops from draft deal
item.description: A cat named Ambition went missing again at COP31 on Thursday. While activists delivered the message with humour, it reflected a serious concern: explicit references to moving away from fossil fuels had disappeared from the latest draft climate agreement. On the eve of the summit's scheduled close, ministers and the Presidency were still trying to bridge sharp differences as civil society groups pressed for stronger action.

item.title: Kenya Says IPCC Report Delay Debate Is About Capacity, Not Politics
item.description: The publication timetable for several climate reports has become one of the most contentious issues at this year’s United Nations climate conference, as several fossil-fuel-dependent countries want to delay the next round of scientific assessments. item.title: Protecting Wildlife Requires Gender Equity
item.description: The recent United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity called for gender-responsive approaches. The United States objected and is the only nation not accepting the plan.
